sentences.headline: When 40% of arrivals bunch into waves, the roster built on the normal timetable delivers 85.1% on time. Re-planning from the live schedule gets back to 91.0% for 104 more staff hours a week.
sentences.flex: Keeping the normal-timetable roster and adding a call-in pool of 4 staff, called when more than 60 AWBs wait for breakdown, does better still: 93.7% on time for 96 call-in hours a week.
sentences.volume: Even with 20% less freight, on-time performance under the normal-timetable roster falls from 94.6% to 93.8% once 40% of flights bunch into waves.
sentences.timezone: Unchecked, the time zone defect alone moves on-time performance by 0.6 points (down), from 93.5% to 92.9%.
sentences.catch: Expediting the riskiest 10% of AWBs at arrival would reach 77% of the shipments that end up late.
sentences.drift: The risk model trained on normal months predicts a 14.3% late rate on the bunched arrivals; the actual rate is 16.9%. Its AUC moves from 0.959 to 0.954.
sentences.roster: On the normal timetable, the optimized roster delivers 94.6% on time against 91.9% for the legacy roster, with 1,354 staff hours a week against 1,456.
